## ✨ Added

- Multi-file shares: pick or drop several files at once. They upload as one end-to-end encrypted bundle under a single link, and the recipient gets the original files back one by one, with no zip. The download page lists them with Download all and, in Chromium over HTTPS, Save to folder.
- Preview before downloading: images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO, APNG, and SVG rendered safely through `<img>`), video (MP4, WebM, OGG, MOV, M4V), audio (MP3, M4A/AAC, OGG, WAV, FLAC, Opus), text and code, and PDF open right on the share page. Decryption happens in the browser and a preview never costs an extra download. Large videos stream progressively through the service worker. Other kinds have a size cap to keep memory in check, and only inert types render, with no SVG or HTML scripting.
- Optional upload protection: set `UPLOAD_PASSWORD` and only people who know it can create shares. Download links stay open to everyone. The server enforces it in constant time and rejects a wrong password before anything is stored. Leave it unset and uploads stay open as before.
- A management link for every share: each new share comes with a secret link (`/m/<slug>#t=…`, shown next to the share link) that lets you delete it before it expires. The server stores only a hash of the token, and the token itself lives in the URL fragment.
- Key verifier for zero-knowledge downloads: a limited or password-protected share now needs proof that the downloader holds the content key before a download is counted or the file is burned. The browser sends `base64url(SHA-256(key))` with the upload, and a download must present a matching `x-fd-key-verifier` header. It is a constant-time, one-way check that never reveals the key. Without it, anyone who learned the slug (for example from a reverse-proxy access log) could use up a limited share and destroy the file without ever being able to decrypt it. Shares created before 1.7.0 have no verifier and behave exactly as before.
- Insecure-context notice: when featherdrop is opened over plain HTTP (for example by IP address), a banner explains that some features are limited there. Large uploads fall back to memory and streamed downloads are off. Over HTTPS the full pipeline is on.

## 🎨 Design

- New house banner with the feather and the wordmark. The README no longer has a separate top heading.

## ⚡ Improved

- Zero-knowledge throughout: the server never sees file contents, names, types, counts, keys or tokens, only opaque blobs and hashes.
- Single-file shares and links created by earlier versions keep working unchanged.
- The streaming video preview plays progressively. Seeking far into a very large video decrypts again from the start, which comes with the sequential encryption. A fully seekable format is a possible next step.
- `UPLOAD_PASSWORD` is in the Unraid template (advanced). Pick a value without leading or trailing spaces.

## 🐛 Fixed

- Large zero-knowledge downloads were broken in the published image. The Next standalone image didn't ship `public/`, so the streaming-download service worker (`/sw-download.js`) returned 404 and every download over 50 MB failed, after the request had already counted against a limited share. `public/` now ships with the image.
- Drag and drop crashed Chrome and Edge. On some Chromium and Edge setups, dropping a file onto the upload area crashed the browser tab with `RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE`. The trigger was the `webkitGetAsEntry()` directory walk that Chromium runs for drag and drop. The file picker and Firefox never use it, which is why both kept working. featherdrop now reads the dropped files straight from the drop event and skips that path entirely.
- Chromium marked downloads as failed: the streamed response declared the ciphertext length as the plaintext `Content-Length`. featherdrop no longer sends a length when it can't know it exactly.
- Abandoned uploads leaked disk space. Interrupted tus uploads that never finished are now swept after 24 hours.
- Cleanup could orphan a file: when deleting an expired file's blob really failed, the database row is now kept so the next sweep tries again, instead of dropping the row and leaving the blob behind.
- The `fd_key` cookie is marked `Secure` when the request came in over HTTPS.
